[size=150][b]Lionheart Fixt 0.18.0 - the Barcelona Attack[/b][/size]

Act 6 is the shortest act in the game and the one with the least left in it: eight maps, 889 live
combatants, and twenty-eight player replies in total, of which two were gated on anything. So this
release is less about unreachable branching than about a city that never reacted to the person walking
through it.

Crossroads Siege is 910 parts and 472 live combatants -- four times the Crypt's Doomed Plateau, the
densest map in the project -- and it shipped with no conversation, no balloon and no dialogue tree at all.
It has three narration lines now, and the relay that makes English soldiers shout while they fight, which
existed on both district maps and not on the one map the English army is actually on.

Two of the act's three quests were never written. "Find Galileo and DaVinci" shipped with a blank Name=
and no states -- the file was created and never filled in -- and the True Cross pursuit has a name and no
states either. Neither was referenced by any map or tree in the game. The blacksmith answers where the two
inventors went now, and because he tells you they were marched out the west gate with a guard who had a
list, the ruts at the western end of the crossroads become evidence rather than scenery: a cracked lens
ground finer than any glazier in Barcelona could manage, and a wax tablet pressed with a hand you have
watched draw. Without having asked him you get the plain line and no reward, which is the right way round.

Then there is the title. "Child Killer" ships complete -- display name Slayer of Innocents, a description,
and a requirements array holding a deliberately false expression, which is how this game marks a perk only
script can grant. Nothing in the game grants it. It is read eight times on the peacetime Gate District and
those reads drive five fully authored dialogue nodes with two replies each, deny it or admit it and
threaten the guard, and none of it has ever fired in any playthrough. Children are not made killable and
that is not what the perk says: they are HP 10000 / AC 1000 in vanilla and they stay that way. The perk's
own words are killing the helpless, and the helpless who can be killed are the citizens at HP 12.

Act 6 is where the consequence was meant to land. The two checker parts the whole mechanism runs on were
already sitting on the siege map, active, carrying the designers' own comments on the polarity, and the act
neither read nor wrote either one. The man searching the district for his son reads them now: a child killer
gets the shipped "Leave me alone! Haven't you done enough?!", and everybody else gets a father asking you to
look for a boy in a red cap. There is a red cap to find, behind a barrel, told to stay where he was put.

Nearby, a relay called "Shy Girl requests help" was sitting active with zero callers, positioning a balloon
over an entity that did not exist and firing a relay that did not exist either. All three pieces are back,
and the consequence end is the map's own: every defender already carries a handler that turns the garrison
on you for attacking a guard. Murdering an unarmed civilian produces no such message, which is exactly what
a witness is for.

Two dying-soldier lines the act never opened are wired, including the Spaniard who tries to give you his
gold -- he hands over the 250 he is talking about. Temple District Siege had 62 dead bodies and not one of
them speaks; six do now.

And the act learns to read you. Surrey O'Connell is an Irish supplies master pressed into feeding the army
that took his country, who calls himself happy to serve the English and begs not to be sent to the Spanish
Inquisition. Show him the clover from the drowned fields of Ireland -- the one the Port District's Irish
sailor hands over -- and the performance stops: take what you need off the Regent's pile, and Surrey
O'Connell never saw a thing. A sworn Inquisitor gets there by a shorter road. Either way the alarm on the
Regent's chest does not fire, which is two new routes past the act's one guarded prize beside the Sneak 100
vanilla shipped. The blacksmith reads your order, your face and your reputation. And the Church Crypt --
thirteen parts, three walls, a lamp, a broken door and one dead guard -- gets the act's first secret, first
trap, first hidden lock and first voice.

[b]Fixt[/b] is a cumulative restoration-and-repair mod for Lionheart, after Fallout Fixt.

Download, unzip, run [i]Mod Manager.bat[/i]. Most of this is level parts, so it needs a character who has not
yet entered act 6 -- and the title needs one who has not yet entered the peacetime districts either.
Unplayed; what you find goes into 0.18.1.

https://github.com/EricHype/LionheartFixt/releases/tag/v0.18.0
